codeReview.summary: Clean, well-structured fix. The panic!("NVS init failed") in open_nvs() has been replaced with an Option<Nvs> return type that returns None on failure after logging a warning. All three main() entry points (normal, sniff, hw-test) correctly handle the new return type with appropriate fallback behavior. The normal mode entry point additionally disables OTA when NVS is unavailable (since flash is consumed by FlashStorage::new regardless of outcome), which is a sensible design decision. The OTA handling in the main loop correctly uses match (ota.as_mut(), ota_buffers.as_mut()) to safely handle the Option-wrapped OTA objects.

sharedStateObservations.observation: FlashStorage::new() consumes the FLASH peripheral unconditionally — even if Nvs::new() fails, the peripheral is not recoverable. This is now documented in open_nvs()'s doc comment, but could be useful in .factory/library/ for future workers modifying NVS-related code.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: app/src/config.rs:119-121 — doc comment noting 'the flash peripheral is consumed by FlashStorage::new() regardless of whether NVS init succeeds. It is not recoverable on failure.'

sharedStateObservations.observation: The hw-test config mode main() sends structured error messages over UART (CONFIG_ERROR:nvs_unavailable) when NVS fails. This pattern of UART status responses could be documented as a convention for the hw-test config receiver protocol.
